newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge rules in favor of assisted suicide.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge rules in favor of assisted suicide.

text.p: A Florida judge Friday gave a man dying of AIDS the right to take his own life with the assistance of his physician.
The state has promised an appeal.

In issuing the decision, Palm Beach County Judge S. Joseph Davis stressed that it applied only to Charles Hall, 35, and to his physician, Dr. Cecil McIver. "This decision only applies to these individuals in this case," he told the court.
The judge also entered the order forbidding the Palm Beach County State Attorney from filing any criminal action against McIver as well as anyone else who might assist him.

Hall, who contracted the AIDS virus 13 years ago via a blood transfusion and was suffering a fourth bout of pneumocystic pneumonia, learned of the decision via a telephone link between the court and his home in Beverly Hills, Fla.
"It does not appear that he has much longer to live," McIver said.

Hall's attorney, Robert Rivas, said his client was overwhelmed and grateful for the ruling. "It took a lot of courage for Judge Davis to rule for us," Rivas said. "He's a tremendous judge with a great deal of experience."

Michael Gross, assistant state attorney general, said Florida would appeal. "This is an issue the Florida Supreme Court will decide ultimately. It is to everyone's best interest to decide it with a finality," he said.
The state's appeal meant that McIver would not be legally free to help Hall commit suicide for a month. Under Florida law, Hall cannot act for 30 days, pending the state's appeal.

Hall and two other terminally ill men sued Florida in Feburary 1996, asking that McIver, a Jupiter, Fla., physician, be spared from prosecution for helping them end their lives if their pain became intolerable.
Robert Cron, 72, and Charles Castonguay, 65, both died of cancer last year and were later dropped as plaintiffs.
